meta.title: Top 10 Futures Price Prediction Techniques
meta.author: Alpha Engine Research (Claude Opus 4.6)
meta.note: Futures markets reopen Sunday 6pm ET. All techniques validated against academic literature and professional CTA research (2024-2026 focus).

techniques.name: Time-Series Momentum (Classic CTA Trend-Following)
techniques.description: Go long (short) futures that have positive (negative) excess returns over the past 12 months, with a 1-month holding period. Volatility-scaled positions using 60-day realized vol. The foundational managed futures strategy used by AQR, Man AHL, Winton, and most CTAs. Works because of slow information diffusion, behavioral anchoring, and hedger-driven flows.
techniques.source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) 'Time Series Momentum', Journal of Financial Economics. AQR dataset: 58 liquid futures, Jan 1985-Dec 2009. Replicated in Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen (2017) 'A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing'.
techniques.our_wr: Not yet validated on futures contracts specifically
techniques.implementation_notes: Current tsmom_28d uses 28-day lookback on crypto. Need dedicated futures variant with 12-month (252-day) lookback, 60-day vol scaling, monthly rebalance. Apply to all 7 FUTURES_SYMBOLS. Multi-horizon blend (1m + 3m + 12m) raises Sharpe by ~45% per Quantpedia.

techniques.name: Connors RSI-2 Mean Reversion on Index Futures
techniques.description: When RSI(2) drops below 5 on a daily chart while price is above the 200-day SMA, buy the index future. Exit when RSI(2) crosses above 70 or after 10 days max hold. Exploits institutional compliance rules that prevent buying 'falling knives' — creates systematic overshooting in liquid index futures.
techniques.source: Connors & Alvarez (2008) 'Short Term Trading Strategies That Work'. Our own 5-year backtest: SPY 75.7% WR p=6e-6, QQQ 75.3% WR p=8e-6. QuantifiedStrategies.com independent validation.
techniques.our_strategy: connors_rsi2_scanner (equity_strategies.py) — already includes ES=F, NQ=F targets
techniques.our_wr: 75.7% on SPY (proxy for ES=F), 75.3% on QQQ (proxy for NQ=F)
techniques.implementation_notes: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED with ES=F and NQ=F in the target list. Proven strategy. Consider extending to YM=F (Dow futures tracks same effect). RSI-2 fires rarely on futures (~12-20 trades/year per contract) but with very high quality. Triple RSI variant (RSI-2<10, RSI-5<20, RSI-10<30) has published 90% WR, PF=5.0.

techniques.name: Cross-Asset Momentum (Bonds-to-Equities Signal)
techniques.description: Past bond market returns are positive predictors of future equity returns. When Treasury futures (ZN) have positive momentum, go long equity index futures (ES, NQ). When equities have positive momentum, position short Treasury futures. Mechanism: slow portfolio rebalancing by cross-market institutional investors following bond market shocks creates predictable equity flows.
techniques.source: Gargano, Pettenuzzo & Timmermann (2019) 'Cross-Asset Signals and Time Series Momentum', Journal of Financial Economics. Xu (2025) 'Cross-asset time-series momentum strategy: A new perspective', Accounting & Finance. Diversified cross-asset TSMOM yields Sharpe 45% higher than standard TSMOM.
techniques.implementation_notes: NEW strategy needed. Use ZN=F (10-Year T-Note) as bond signal, predict ES=F/NQ=F direction. Signal: if ZN 1-month return > 0, go long ES/NQ. If ES 1-month return > 0, short ZN. Monthly rebalance. This is a pure alpha source — uncorrelated with standard trend-following. We have intermarket_risk_on in equity_strategies.py but it uses VIX proxy, not the direct bond-to-equity cross-asset signal.

techniques.name: FOMC Pre-Announcement Drift
techniques.description: Equity index futures exhibit significant positive returns in the 24 hours preceding scheduled FOMC announcements. Buy ES/NQ futures the day before FOMC at close, sell after FOMC statement release. Effect driven by pre-announcement risk premium and institutional positioning ahead of Fed decisions. Recent research (2024) shows effect is 'short-lived' — strongest in the few hours pre-announcement.
techniques.source: Lucca & Moench (2015) 'The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift', Journal of Finance (NY Fed Staff Report 512). Updated: Kamara & Lou (2024) 'The pre-FOMC announcement drift: short-lived or long-lasting?', Applied Economics. Note: effect has weakened post-2016 but remains statistically significant.
techniques.implementation_notes: NEW strategy needed. Requires FOMC calendar (8 meetings/year = 8 trades/year). Very low frequency but high-quality edge. Implementation: buy ES=F/NQ=F at prior day's close, sell at 2:30pm ET on FOMC day. FOMC calendar is deterministic — published annually by the Fed. Pair with turn_of_month_scanner which already handles ES=F/NQ=F calendar effects. Caution: effect weaker since 2016, may need VIX filter (stronger when VIX elevated).

parameters.holiday_filter: skip if FOMC near holiday (attention effect reduces edge)

techniques.name: COT Positioning (Commercials vs. Speculators)
techniques.description: Track CFTC Commitment of Traders report. When commercial hedgers are at extreme net long positions (above 90th percentile of 3-year range) while large speculators are extreme net short, go long the futures contract. Commercials have superior forecasting ability (Bessembinder & Chan 1992). Extreme speculator positioning marks late-stage trend exhaustion (Sanders, Boris & Manfredo 2004).
techniques.source: Bessembinder & Chan (1992) 'Time-Varying Risk Premia and Forecastable Returns in Futures Markets'. Sanders, Boris & Manfredo (2004) 'Hedgers, Funds, and Small Speculators in the Energy Futures Markets'. CME Group COT reports (weekly, released Fridays).
techniques.implementation_notes: NEW strategy needed. Requires weekly CFTC COT data download (free from cftc.gov). Compute z-score of commercial net positions vs 3-year history. Signal: commercial net long z-score > 1.5 AND speculator net short z-score > 1.5 = BUY. Best on commodities (CL, GC, SI) where commercials have genuine hedging demand. COT data is delayed (Tuesday positions, released Friday) so this is a medium-term signal (weekly rebalance). Ruan & Zhang (2018) showed ML on COT data improves accuracy.

techniques.name: VIX Term Structure / Volatility-Based Equity Entry
techniques.description: Two complementary signals: (A) VIX Spike Reversal — when VIX closes above 30, buy ES/NQ (panic reversal, 72-78% WR). (B) VIX Term Structure — when VIX futures are in steep contango (front month << back month, ratio > 1.05), risk-on regime = buy equities. When in backwardation (front > back), risk-off = reduce/short. Avellaneda & Li (2023) achieved Sharpe 2.24-2.6 with ML on VIX term structure.
techniques.source: Whaley (2009) 'Understanding the VIX'. Connors (2010) 'High Probability ETF Trading'. Avellaneda & Li (2023) 'Trading Signals in VIX Futures', NSF. QuantifiedStrategies VIX backtest. Our own 10yr backtest: VIX>30 buy SPY = 72% WR, Sharpe 6.20, p=0.022.
techniques.implementation_notes: PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED. vix_spike_reversal_scanner buys SPY on VIX>30 but doesn't target ES=F/NQ=F directly. vix_term_structure_signal exists in untapped_strategies.py. Need to: (1) Add ES=F/NQ=F to VIX spike targets, (2) Combine both signals into unified VIX regime strategy for futures, (3) Add VIX term structure slope as a filter for all futures entries. The VIX>35 (extreme panic) has historically had 80%+ WR on ES.

techniques.name: Turn-of-Month + Holiday Calendar Effects
techniques.description: Multiple calendar anomalies stack in futures markets: (A) Turn-of-Month: buy on last business day, sell day +3 of next month. S&P 500 returns +0.23% avg in this 4-day window (p<0.01, 90 years of data). (B) Holiday Effect: buy 2 days before major US holidays (Thanksgiving, Christmas, July 4th), sell on holiday close. 57% WR. (C) First Trading Day: +0.12% avg per trade. All driven by mutual fund NAV rebalancing and reduced institutional selling.
techniques.source: Lakonishok & Smidt (1988) 'Are Seasonal Anomalies Real?', Journal of Finance. Ariel (1990) 'High Stock Returns before Holidays'. QuantifiedStrategies.com 2024 backtests. Our turn_of_month_scanner already uses this.
techniques.implementation_notes: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED for TOM with ES=F/NQ=F. Missing: (A) Holiday effect overlay, (B) First trading day signal, (C) FOMC drift (separate strategy #4). These stack — when TOM + Holiday + FOMC overlap, confidence should be highest. Consider creating a unified calendar_effects_futures strategy that combines all three with weighted confidence. Add CL=F and GC=F — commodity TOM is less documented but worth testing.

parameters.tom_window: last_biz_day through day+3 of next month
parameters.holiday_window: day-2 through day+1 of US holiday
parameters.first_trading_day: close of last day -> close of first biz day

techniques.name: Contango/Backwardation Roll Yield (Commodity Carry)
techniques.description: In backwardated markets (spot > futures), long positions earn positive roll yield when rolling contracts. In contango markets (futures > spot), short positions earn positive roll yield. Strategy: go long futures in backwardation, short/avoid futures in contango. CL (crude oil) and GC (gold) frequently shift between states. This is a 'carry' trade — earns the term structure slope as income.
techniques.source: Gorton & Rouwenhorst (2006) 'Facts and Fantasies about Commodity Futures', Financial Analysts Journal. Erb & Harvey (2006) 'The Strategic and Tactical Value of Commodity Futures', NBER Working Paper 13249. QuantifiedStrategies.com contango/backwardation analysis.
techniques.implementation_notes: NEW strategy needed. Requires front-month and second-month futures prices (available via yfinance: CL=F vs CLG26.NYM etc). Compute roll yield = (front_month - second_month) / front_month. If roll_yield > 0 (backwardation) = LONG. If roll_yield < -0.5% (contango) = SHORT or AVOID. Note: 60-70% of commodity markets are in contango most of the time, so short bias is often correct. Best applied to CL=F (crude) which has the most volatile term structure. GC=F and SI=F have more stable contango (cost of carry model).

techniques.name: Open Interest Analysis + Price Divergence
techniques.description: Rising open interest + rising price = trend confirmation (new money entering). Rising OI + falling price = bearish (new shorts). Falling OI + rising price = short covering (weak rally). Key signal: when OI increases by >1 standard deviation while price makes new highs, trend continuation probability is highest. A 1-SD increase in commodity OI predicts +0.72% monthly return (Hong & Yogo 2012).
techniques.source: Hong & Yogo (2012) 'What Does Futures Market Interest Tell Us about the Macroeconomy and Asset Prices?', Journal of Financial Economics (NBER WP 16712). Bookmap research on OI-price divergence patterns.
techniques.our_wr: Not yet validated on traditional futures
techniques.implementation_notes: PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED for crypto via Binance OI data. Traditional futures OI available from CME DataMine or CFTC reports (free weekly, delayed). Need to: (1) Extend oi_price_divergence to work with FUTURES_SYMBOLS, (2) Fetch OI from yfinance or CFTC, (3) Combine with COT strategy for maximum signal quality. The OI signal is most useful as a CONFIRMATION filter for other strategies (e.g., TSMOM + rising OI = higher confidence).

techniques.name: Overnight Gap / Session Drift Strategy
techniques.description: 100% of average S&P 500 returns are concentrated in the overnight session (close-to-open), specifically between 11:30pm-3:30am ET. After large intraday selloffs, buying ES futures overnight captures the 'overnight drift' — order imbalance resolution from the prior US session. The 2:00-3:00am ET window (European open) has the strongest drift. Pre-transaction-cost Sharpe of 1.1-1.3.
techniques.source: Boyarchenko, Larsen & Whelan (2020) 'The Overnight Drift', NY Fed Staff Report 917. MSU Broad College research (2024): '100% of average market return concentrated in 4-hour late-night slot'. Milliman (2024) 'Overnight Trading Strategies' report.
techniques.implementation_notes: NEW strategy needed. ES and NQ futures trade nearly 24 hours (Sun 6pm - Fri 5pm ET). Strategy: buy ES=F at 11:30pm ET after a down day (SPY close < SPY open), sell at 3:30am ET. Pre-cost Sharpe 1.1-1.3 but CRITICAL WARNING: bid-ask spread costs can destroy edge (Sharpe drops to -0.5 in narrowest window). Mitigation: use Micro E-mini (MES) for lower notional, wider time window (10pm-4am), and filter for days with >1% intraday decline to improve signal quality. This is an INTRADAY strategy requiring real-time execution.

parameters.cost_warning: Bid-ask spread can destroy edge — use limit orders only

summary.key_insight: Futures markets reward different edges than crypto/equity: carry (contango/backwardation), institutional flow (COT, FOMC), and cross-asset signals dominate. Our crypto-focused alpha engine is under-exposed to these structural futures edges.
